mechanism_narrative: Increasing GDP indicates strong economic activity, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are negative when GDP growth is positive.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment suggests economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are positive when unemployment rises.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment and high Fed Funds indicate tight monetary policy, leading to negative returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive under tight monetary policy.

mechanism_narrative: Rising Fed Funds in a tightening cycle predict negative S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are positive when Fed Funds rise above 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production signals strong supply, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are negative when industrial production grows.

mechanism_narrative: Rising CPI suggests inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns in 20 days.
failure_condition: 20-day returns are positive when CPI increases by >2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing employment and housing starts signal economic strength, leading to positive S&P 500 returns in 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day returns are negative when employment and housing starts increase.

mechanism_narrative: Rising retail sales in late-cycle expansion predict positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: 60-day returns are negative when retail sales grow by >5% YoY.
